stem.text: Hydrogen and deuterium can be represented by the nuclide symbols ${}^{1}_{1}\text{H}$ and ${}^{2}_{1}\text{H}$ respectively.
What is a difference between hydrogen and deuterium?

A.text: The deuterium atom has twice the number of electrons as the hydrogen atom.

B.text: The deuterium nucleus has a charge, but the hydrogen nucleus has no charge.

C.text: The deuterium nucleus has less mass than the hydrogen nucleus.

D.text: The deuterium nucleus has half the charge per unit mass of the hydrogen nucleus.
